statement: The proposed change at FILE.pipelines/ingestion/src/main/scala/newspipe/application/ports/Ports.scala, FILE.pipelines/ingestion/src/main/scala/newspipe/application/services/IngestionService.scala, FILE.pipelines/ingestion/src/main/scala/newspipe/infrastructure/rss/RomeRssClient.scala and FILE.conf/feeds.conf — add a deterministic manifest-driven source scanner and validator that exposes usable feeds through the existing RssSource port — satisfies RSS/Atom validation for a large candidate manifest without violating the hexagonal port boundary, the NewsPipe-only execution lifecycle, or the no-LLM-in-scanning constraint.
justification: The baseline DTR shows an existing RssSource port consumed by IngestionService and implemented by RomeRssClient, which already performs HttpClient fetch with redirect/timeout and Rome SyndFeedInput parsing; manifest and result handling can use the circe and Typesafe config dependencies already on the ingestion classpath. conf/feeds.conf is currently a flat list with no publisher/provenance or validation status, and no status type exists in ingestion main sources, so the scanner is additive creation work rather than a redesign. The launcher starts pipelines with sbt run and contains no external scheduler, so validation can live in NewsPipe execution. Ingestion has no opencode/LLM calls; enrichment configuration already pins nvidia/* models and keeps per-item opencode run in its own adapter, confirming that batching is a separate constraint and not part of this scanner. Stage 1 evidence: all seven experiments (port extension point, Rome/HttpClient reuse, existing circe/config dependencies, flat manifest gap, in-process lifecycle, LLM-free ingestion with nvidia/* enrichment models, absent status types) passed; the RED verdict is a 0.03125 gate gap with no failing breakpoints, so the revised prior reflects that complete evidence set.
